title: Data Sufficiency Mastery
tagline: Year 4 — All four outcomes with numbers, percentages, ratios and yes/no questions; a quick decision procedure

introduction.overview: Data sufficiency asks whether given statements are enough to answer a question. Mastery means deciding quickly and correctly in all four outcomes: I alone, II alone, both together, neither. The procedure is the same each time: list the unknowns, test statement I alone by trying to find two different answers, test II the same way, and combine only if both fail. For yes/no questions the answer must be always yes or always no.
introduction.placementRelevance: Data sufficiency is common in management-oriented tests and in the advanced DI and reasoning sections.
introduction.realWorldContext: Deciding whether you have enough information before committing to a decision is the real-world skill.

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: A statement is sufficient only if it leads to a single answer in every situation it allows.

coreDefinitions: Insufficient: more than one answer possible.
Consistent yes/no: always yes or always no.
Redundant: adds nothing to the other.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Picture every situation the statement permits. If they all agree, it suffices.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Try to build two worlds with different answers for I; then for II; then for I and II together.

mainNarrative: Company A sold ₹40 lakh and B sold 25% more: B sold 50, total 90. "B sold more than 45" leaves 46, 47, …; only I is sufficient.
"x² > y²" for positive whole numbers means x > y, so it settles "is x greater than y?"; "x + y = 10" does not.
"n is divisible by 12" leaves 12, 24, 36, 48; "n is divisible by 18" leaves 18, 36; together n = 36.
A rectangle with perimeter 24 has l + w = 12; area 36 gives l = w = 6 only when both hold: together they show a square.
Where a yes/no answer varies across the permitted worlds, the statement is insufficient.

deepDiveAspects.title: Hidden constraints
deepDiveAspects.content: Check the ranges in the setup: they can make a statement sufficient.

deepDiveAspects.title: Both together but not enough
deepDiveAspects.content: Two statements can overlap so much that they still leave several possibilities.

solvedExamples.title: I alone
solvedExamples.question: A sold ₹40 lakh. I. B sold 25% more than A. II. B sold more than ₹45 lakh. Total of A and B?
solvedExamples.finalAnswer: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not

solvedExamples.title: Both needed
solvedExamples.question: n ≤ 50. I. n is divisible by 12. II. n is divisible by 18. What is n?
solvedExamples.finalAnswer: Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient

solvedExamples.title: Yes/no
solvedExamples.question: x, y positive whole numbers. I. x² > y². Is x > y?

steps.title: Squares
steps.explanation: For positive numbers x² > y² means x > y.

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Try to find two different answers under I, then under II, then under both.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: If statements repeat, together adds nothing.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: You never need the exact answer.

easy.question:
Company A had sales of ₹40 lakh in 2023. Company B's sales b are a whole number of lakh, at most 100.

Question: What were the combined sales of A and B?
I. B's sales were 25% more than A's.
II. B's sales were more than ₹45 lakh.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
Even both statements together are not sufficient
easy.correctAnswer: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
easy.explanation: Statement I alone fixes the answer as 90. Statement II alone leaves several answers possible (for example 86 and 87). Taken together they fix the answer as 90. Answer: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not.

easy.question:
x and y are whole numbers from 1 to 9.

Question: Is x greater than y?
I. x² is greater than y².
II. x + y = 10.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
Even both statements together are not sufficient
easy.correctAnswer: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
easy.explanation: Statement I alone fixes the answer as Yes. Statement II alone leaves several answers possible (for example No and Yes). Taken together they fix the answer as Yes. Answer: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not.

easy.question:
The monthly incomes of X and Y (in thousands) are multiples of 10 from 10 to 60.

Question: Does X earn more than Y?
I. X earns ₹20 thousand more than Y.
II. X earns ₹40 thousand.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
Even both statements together are not sufficient
Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
easy.correctAnswer: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
easy.explanation: Statement I alone fixes the answer as Yes. Statement II alone leaves several answers possible (for example Yes and No). Taken together they fix the answer as Yes. Answer: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not.

intermediate.question:
An article was bought for ₹100, ₹200, ₹300 or ₹400 and sold for a multiple of ₹10 from ₹100 to ₹700.

Question: Is the profit percentage more than 20%?
I. The selling price was ₹300.
II. The cost price was ₹200 and the selling price was more than ₹250.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
Even both statements together are not sufficient
intermediate.correctAnswer: Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
intermediate.explanation: Statement I alone leaves several answers possible (for example Yes and No). Statement II alone fixes the answer as Yes. Taken together they fix the answer as Yes. Answer: Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not.

intermediate.question:
Old sales and new sales are each one of 100, 200, 300, 400 or 500.

Question: What was the percentage increase in sales?
I. The new sales were 300.
II. The new sales were 50% more than the old sales.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
Even both statements together are not sufficient
Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
intermediate.correctAnswer: Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
intermediate.explanation: Statement I alone leaves several answers possible (for example 200 and 50). Statement II alone fixes the answer as 50. Taken together they fix the answer as 50. Answer: Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not.

intermediate.question:
Three numbers a, b and c are whole numbers from 1 to 9.

Question: What is the average of a, b and c?
I. a + b = 10.
II. c = 4.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
Even both statements together are not sufficient
Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
intermediate.correctAnswer: Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
intermediate.explanation: Statement I alone leaves several answers possible (for example 3.67 and 4). Statement II alone leaves several answers possible (for example 2 and 2.33). Taken together they fix the answer as 4.67. Answer: Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient.

advanced.question:
A rectangle has whole-number sides l and w from 1 to 10 (in cm).

Question: Is the rectangle a square?
I. Its perimeter is 24 cm.
II. Its area is 36 square cm.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
Even both statements together are not sufficient
advanced.correctAnswer: Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
advanced.explanation: Statement I alone leaves several answers possible (for example No and Yes). Statement II alone leaves several answers possible (for example No and Yes). Taken together they fix the answer as Yes. Answer: Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient.

advanced.question:
A school has n students (50, 100 or 150) and p of them passed, where p is a multiple of 10 not exceeding n.

Question: Did more than 60% of the students pass?
I. 90 students passed.
II. The school has 150 students.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
Even both statements together are not sufficient
advanced.correctAnswer: Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
advanced.explanation: Statement I alone leaves several answers possible (for example Yes and No). Statement II alone leaves several answers possible (for example No and Yes). Taken together they fix the answer as No. Answer: Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient.

placementStyle.question:
Ravi's marks in two tests are each a multiple of 10 from 0 to 100.

Question: What is Ravi's total mark in the two tests?
I. He scored 70 in the first test.
II. The average of his two marks is 80.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
Even both statements together are not sufficient
placementStyle.correctAnswer: Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
placementStyle.explanation: Statement I alone leaves several answers possible (for example 70 and 80). Statement II alone fixes the answer as 160. Taken together they fix the answer as 160. Answer: Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not.

placementStyle.question:
Department A has a employees and department B has b employees; each is a multiple of 10 from 10 to 60.

Question: How many employees does department B have?
I. Department A has 30 employees.
II. Department B has more than 20 employees.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Even both statements together are not sufficient
Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
placementStyle.correctAnswer: Even both statements together are not sufficient
placementStyle.explanation: Statement I alone leaves several answers possible (for example 10 and 20). Statement II alone leaves several answers possible (for example 30 and 40). Taken together they still leave several answers possible (for example 30 and 40). Answer: Even both statements together are not sufficient.

placementStyle.question:
x and y are whole numbers from 1 to 30.

Question: What is the HCF of x and y?
I. x = 12 and y = 18.
II. x + y = 30.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
Both statements together are needed; neither alone is sufficient
Even both statements together are not sufficient
Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
placementStyle.correctAnswer: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not
placementStyle.explanation: Statement I alone fixes the answer as 6. Statement II alone leaves several answers possible (for example 1 and 2). Taken together they fix the answer as 6. Answer: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not.
